comment: Every file in the chain that produces a corrected image, pinned. A name, a length and four digests are measurements of a file rather than any part of it, and a digest reconstructs nothing. Nothing here carries a byte of any cartridge, translation or patch.
decides: sha256 decides. The size rejects a wrong file for one stat call, and crc32, md5 and sha1 are published beside it so a copy can be cross-checked against a catalogue that keys on any of them. None of those three decides anything on its own: crc32 is a 32-bit error code, and md5 and sha1 are both collision-broken.

editions.name: japanese
editions.summary: neviksti's patch on the Japanese original, decompressed to ninety six megabit.
editions.reads: Star Ocean (J) SDD1 Patched (Hack) v1 Neviksti.sfc

supersedes.why: What this correction writes changed on 2026-10-28, because it declared chipset 0x00, which removes the battery along with the S-DD1. Star Ocean saves to battery-backed memory, and bsnes keeps save RAM only for a declared battery. snes-rom-image-python fixed the rule in 40539b4: taking the coprocessor out of 0x45 leaves 0x02, RAM and a battery. The digests above are what this tool produced while writing 0x00.

What this correction writes changed on 2026-08-25, because the checksum it writes was wrong for an image whose length is not a power of two, and both of these are twelve megabytes. snes-rom-image-python fixed the rule in d9ccd39: the development manual says the remainder is added repeatedly until the total reaches a power of two, and following it took agreement with real cartridges from 2,150 of 2,780 retail images to 2,768. The digests above are what this tool produced while carrying the old rule. An image matching them carries a checksum no cartridge would.
